minutes.summary: Consultants and the developer's side disputed whether the project is economic under the return-on-total-cost test and how much sewer privilege fee it can bear. The board also went through draft decision conditions and waivers.

what_happened.line: The Zoning Board of Appeals closed the 40B hearing by voice vote.
The applicant is to waive the statutory decision clock by letter, extending the deadline to January 30th.
A sewer fee compromise was left to offline talks among the applicant, town counsel and the consultant, with the sewer commission and selectmen possibly brought in.
A continued session was set for December 10th at eight o'clock, when the fee talks are to be reported back.
The applicant's engineer is to contact the fire chief to confirm his concerns are resolved before the decision.

why_it_matters: The sewer privilege fee decides how much this project pays toward a sewer system the town still carries debt on, and any reduction would shift that cost toward the town's sewer users and the town budget, mostly taxes.
The fee gap also bears on whether the project is economic at all, and a denial or contested conditions could lead to an appeal with legal costs falling on the town.
